authority_limit: These sources define observation/measurement models, not enterprise acceptance authority or all metrological law.
bounded_claim: Observation standards distinguish the observation act, feature/property being observed, procedure/sensor, and result; a result cannot be interpreted without the observation context.
negative_twin: A numeric result with no observed-property/procedure context can be syntactically valid while semantically unusable.

authority_limit: Unit standards do not define business meaning, source truth or calibration status.
bounded_claim: Quantity kind, dimension, unit and numerical magnitude are distinct concepts; conversions are valid only under compatible quantity/dimension and scale laws.
negative_twin: The value 100 with a unit code cannot be safely compared to another 100 if quantity kinds or scale semantics differ.

authority_limit: Metrology sources do not prescribe domain-specific acceptance limits.
bounded_claim: Measurement uncertainty, measurement error, tolerance and decision limits are distinct; uncertainty characterizes dispersion associated with a result and is not an observed error value.
negative_twin: A result can satisfy a tolerance while having uncertainty too large for a defensible conformity decision.

authority_limit: These sources do not certify any particular instrument occurrence.
bounded_claim: Calibration establishes a relation between indications and reference quantity values under stated conditions; it is not equivalent to unit conversion or normalization.
negative_twin: Converting Celsius to kelvin does not demonstrate that a temperature sensor is calibrated.

authority_limit: Traceability to measurement references does not itself prove business-process provenance or result acceptance.
bounded_claim: Metrological traceability requires a documented unbroken calibration chain to references, with uncertainty contributions, not merely a provenance link or device identifier.
negative_twin: A sensor model and serial number can be known while its current calibration chain is absent or expired.

authority_limit: Sampling standards do not supply statistical representativeness or inferential validity automatically.
bounded_claim: Sampling features and ultimate features of interest are distinct; observations on samples require explicit relationships to the population/object being inferred about.
negative_twin: A lab result from a sample cannot silently be treated as a direct observation of an entire batch or patient.

authority_limit: FHIR and policy/schema sources define specific models, not universal cohort semantics.
bounded_claim: Definitional group criteria and enumerated membership are distinct; a population rule may exist without a materialized member list and a list may not encode the generating rule.
negative_twin: A cached cohort member list can be stale even when its original predicate remains unchanged.

authority_limit: Clinical-trial standards do not define every business or observational population.
bounded_claim: Analytical results require an explicit target population/estimand and traceability to analysis data; population semantics are part of the meaning of an estimate, not presentation metadata.
negative_twin: The same estimator applied to ITT and per-protocol populations can produce equally well-formed but semantically different results.

authority_limit: Observation standards do not guarantee statistical representativeness.
bounded_claim: Sample identity and target population are distinct, and inferential support depends on how the sample relates to the population.
negative_twin: A convenience sample may be exactly recorded yet fail to support a population claim.

authority_limit: These sources do not prescribe one denominator rule across domains.
bounded_claim: Denominator or risk-set/support semantics must be explicit for rates, proportions and time-to-event results; cardinality alone does not define who was eligible to contribute.
negative_twin: Two rates can have the same numerator and row grain but different denominators and therefore different meaning.

authority_limit: Policy and reporting standards define their own constraint models, not universal applicability truth.
bounded_claim: Applicability may be restricted by explicit contextual constraints/dimensions; constraints are not equivalent to authority, identity or representation.
negative_twin: A policy can be structurally valid but not apply because jurisdiction, purpose or segment constraints fail.

authority_limit: These sources do not impose one global versioning mechanism.
bounded_claim: Population/cohort definitions and materialized memberships require edition/cut identity so later data changes cannot silently rewrite the population used by an analysis.
negative_twin: Re-running the same named cohort query after source corrections can change membership while preserving the cohort name.

authority_limit: ODRL defines digital rights policies, not all legal or organizational norms.
bounded_claim: Permission, prohibition and duty are independent normative constructs; duties can constrain permissions and must not be inferred from absence of prohibition.
negative_twin: No prohibition record does not imply permission, and a permission may still carry an unfulfilled duty.

authority_limit: XACML processing does not prove policy issuer legitimacy, obligation fulfillment or external effect completion.
bounded_claim: Authorization decisions, obligations and advice are distinct outputs with explicit combining/delegation semantics.
negative_twin: A Permit decision can be returned with an obligation that the enforcement point fails to discharge.

authority_limit: FHIR/DPV/ODRL do not establish jurisdiction-specific legal validity by themselves.
bounded_claim: Consent directives and privacy permissions/restrictions are normative artifacts with provenance and scope; the existence of a consent record is not proof that every intended use is permitted.
negative_twin: A signed consent can be valid for one purpose and prohibited for another.

authority_limit: NIST controls are not automatic legal mandates outside the selected governance context.
bounded_claim: A control requirement and a tailored profile are normative declarations; implementation and assessment evidence are separate objects.
negative_twin: A control can be required in a profile while not implemented or while assessment evidence is stale.

authority_limit: OSCAL models evidence exchange but does not itself certify system security.
bounded_claim: Declared implementation, planned assessment and observed assessment result are separate lifecycle states; fulfillment cannot be inferred from obligation declaration.
negative_twin: A control implementation statement may exist while an assessment result records a finding.

authority_limit: These standards do not define every enterprise waiver process.
bounded_claim: Exceptions/waivers and consequences/remedies require explicit scope and authority; they are not equivalent to deleting the original obligation.
negative_twin: A time-bounded waiver can suspend enforcement without erasing the underlying requirement or its audit history.

authority_limit: PROV records asserted provenance relations; it does not prove the truth or causal sufficiency of those assertions.
bounded_claim: Provenance distinguishes entities, activities and agents plus generation, usage, derivation, attribution and invalidation relations.
negative_twin: A complete provenance graph can faithfully describe production of an incorrect result.

authority_limit: OpenLineage describes operational lineage, not semantic authority or business truth.
bounded_claim: OpenLineage keeps Job, Run and Dataset identities distinct and attaches different facets to each.
negative_twin: Two runs of the same job can consume different dataset versions and yield different outputs.

authority_limit: Clinical standards do not prescribe lineage for all enterprise analytics.
bounded_claim: Analysis standards require traceability among source/tabulation data, analysis datasets, metadata and reported results.
negative_twin: A table value can be numerically reproducible yet fail review if its derivation to source and analysis metadata is missing.

authority_limit: DCAT/DWBP are web-data models and best practices, not all storage systems.
bounded_claim: Dataset identity, distribution/representation and provenance/usage are separable; publishing another distribution does not create a new semantic dataset by default.
negative_twin: The same dataset can have CSV and Parquet distributions with different bytes but one semantic publication identity.

authority_limit: These models do not define all retention or legal deletion obligations.
bounded_claim: Correction, invalidation and supersession are provenance events that preserve the historical derivation rather than erasing it.
negative_twin: A corrected result should not make the prior issued result disappear from audit provenance.

authority_limit: Provenance standards intentionally do not grant domain authority.
bounded_claim: Knowing where data came from is distinct from deciding whether that source was authoritative for the semantic claim.
negative_twin: A derived dataset can correctly cite a spreadsheet source that was never the system of record.

authority_limit: FHIR and clinical guidance do not define every analytic method.
bounded_claim: Observed facts and predicted risks/estimates are distinct epistemic objects even when both are represented numerically.
negative_twin: A 0.8 predicted probability of an event is not an observation that the event occurred.

authority_limit: ONNX/FMI define model interchange/execution contracts, not factual truth of model outputs.
bounded_claim: A model artifact/version and an execution of that model are distinct; runtime mode, operator set or simulation configuration can change result interpretation.
negative_twin: Two executions of the same model version with different inputs or solver settings produce different occurrences.

authority_limit: HLA/FMI define simulation interoperability, not model validity for every use.
bounded_claim: Simulation federation and co-simulation outputs are executions of abstractions and must not silently become observations of real-world state.
negative_twin: A synthetic failure scenario can be useful evidence without implying the failure happened in production.

authority_limit: Statistical standards do not make an estimate causally valid merely by computation.
bounded_claim: An estimate is tied to an estimand/population/model and is epistemically distinct from observed input data.
negative_twin: A regression estimate can be precise while its identifying assumptions are false.

authority_limit: These sources do not define all causal inference frameworks.
bounded_claim: Hypothetical/counterfactual quantities and realized outcomes require different status and provenance.
negative_twin: A modeled treatment-policy counterfactual is not a recorded patient outcome.

authority_limit: Control-chart/reference standards do not define business authority for choosing a target.
bounded_claim: Targets, limits and reference values are normative/reference constructs and must not be represented as observed states.
negative_twin: A target temperature of 20°C is not evidence that the measured temperature is 20°C.

authority_limit: These sources do not define a universal recommendation workflow.
bounded_claim: A recommendation or analytical finding is not an authorized decision or executed effect; epistemic output and authority/effect boundaries remain separate.
negative_twin: A high-risk prediction can recommend review while policy authority still denies action.

authority_limit: These sources define causal-inference semantics and frameworks, not a universal domain treatment policy.
bounded_claim: Causal contrasts answer intervention/counterfactual questions and are not interchangeable with associations observed between exposed and unexposed groups.
negative_twin: A strong predictive association may remain noncausal under confounding.

authority_limit: A graph does not make its assumptions true and does not identify effects when required assumptions fail.
bounded_claim: A causal graph encodes causal and subject-matter assumptions used for identification; it is not merely a graph-topology or temporal-order relation.
negative_twin: Two variables can be connected in a dependency graph without either being a valid intervention cause of the other.

authority_limit: Assignment semantics do not prove adherence, outcome measurement quality or causal assumptions after protocol deviations.
bounded_claim: Treatment-assignment mechanism is part of the causal design/identification contract; random assignment and covariate-conditioned observational assignment have different guarantees.
negative_twin: The same observed treatment groups can support different causal claims depending on how assignment occurred.

authority_limit: Specifying an estimand does not make it identifiable, estimable, unbiased or policy-relevant.
bounded_claim: The causal effect/estimand of interest must be specified independently of the statistical estimator and resulting numerical estimate.
negative_twin: Two estimators can target one estimand, while one estimator can be applied to different estimands under changed population/intercurrent-event strategies.

authority_limit: Identification under stated assumptions does not establish assumption truth or implementation correctness.
bounded_claim: Causal identification depends on explicit assumptions and can target effects for specific populations; numerical estimation follows only after an effect is identified under those assumptions.
negative_twin: A low-variance estimator can precisely estimate an associational quantity when the desired causal estimand is not identified.

authority_limit: These frameworks do not provide automatic transportability beyond their target populations and assumptions.
bounded_claim: A causal effect is scoped to a target population/subpopulation and assignment/intervention semantics; effects such as local average treatment effects cannot silently generalize to all subjects.
negative_twin: A valid complier-average effect can differ from the average treatment effect in the full eligible population.

authority_limit: Cryptographic RBG standards do not define all statistical simulation or experimental assignment requirements.
bounded_claim: Entropy sources, deterministic random-bit generators and complete random-bit-generator constructions are distinct components with separate validation obligations.
negative_twin: A deterministic generator can replay perfectly from state while providing no fresh entropy.

authority_limit: Reproducing a pseudorandom stream does not prove distributional suitability or scientific validity.
bounded_claim: Reproducible pseudorandom execution depends on generator kind/version and explicit seed/state/stream construction, not just a generic random flag.
negative_twin: The same integer seed under different generator algorithms or versions can produce different streams.

authority_limit: Random assignment does not prove adherence, blinding success or outcome validity.
bounded_claim: A randomization schedule/mechanism is distinct from each realized treatment assignment and from treatment actually received; the schedule must be preplanned and reproducible where required.
negative_twin: A subject can be randomly assigned treatment A yet receive treatment B or no treatment.

authority_limit: Random-number standards do not define epistemic uncertainty semantics.
bounded_claim: A mechanism that generates random/pseudorandom values is an execution process with state and provenance; a probability distribution or uncertainty interval is a semantic description and need not imply such a mechanism.
negative_twin: A fixed analytic probability distribution can be evaluated deterministically, while a simulation can draw random samples from it.

authority_limit: NIST differential-privacy guidance does not validate a particular implementation merely because it adds noise.
bounded_claim: Differentially private algorithms commonly rely on deliberately randomized noise mechanisms whose mechanism and parameters affect the guarantee; random noise is not generic measurement error.
negative_twin: Adding arbitrary random noise can reduce utility without satisfying a differential-privacy guarantee.

authority_limit: Spawn construction does not prove independence for arbitrary custom generators or scientific workflows.
bounded_claim: Parallel/substream construction is a distinct semantic obligation: child streams require a documented derivation/independence posture rather than thread-local guessing.
negative_twin: Two workers initialized with accidentally identical state can appear independent while emitting identical pseudorandom sequences.

authority_limit: Currency codes do not provide valuation method, exchange rate, legal ownership or accounting policy.
bounded_claim: Monetary numeric facts require explicit currency/unit semantics; ISO 4217 currency identity and minor-unit relationships are part of interpretation rather than formatting.
negative_twin: 100 USD and 100 EUR have equal numeric magnitude but are not equal monetary values without an explicit conversion relation and time/basis.

authority_limit: Money datatypes do not establish price source, valuation authority or settlement finality.
bounded_claim: Financial standards model Money as an amount plus currency; the numeric component alone is semantically incomplete.
negative_twin: The decimal 10.00 without currency cannot be safely compared, aggregated or settled as a monetary amount.

authority_limit: FHIR/XBRL do not define every enterprise rate convention.
bounded_claim: Ratios/rates preserve numerator and denominator/basis semantics and must not be flattened into a dimensionless scalar merely because serialization is numeric.
negative_twin: 5 mg/10 mL and 0.5 mg/mL can be numerically transformable while retaining different declared numerator/denominator provenance and precision.

authority_limit: EPCIS quantity semantics apply to its supply-chain objects, not all count/measure models.
bounded_claim: Counts and physical measure amounts are distinct: GS1 EPCIS uses an omitted UOM for positive-integer counts and a UOM for variable physical measures.
negative_twin: A quantity of 10 can mean ten items or ten kilograms; magnitude and object class alone do not choose the semantics.

authority_limit: The cited standards provide domain examples rather than one universal percentage convention.
bounded_claim: Rates, percentages and monetary amounts require explicit quantitative conventions/bases; a decimal representation such as 0.05 does not by itself state whether the semantic value is 5%, a unitless ratio, a rate, or an amount.
negative_twin: 0.05 can be a 5% premium rate, a probability, a unitless ratio or a physical coefficient with different comparison/aggregation laws.

authority_limit: Reporting and healthcare datatype standards do not define every quantitative business concept.
bounded_claim: A quantitative fact is interpreted with concept/kind, unit/currency and contextual basis; formatting or raw numeric equality does not determine quantitative equality.
negative_twin: Two facts with identical decimals but different units, currencies, concepts or ratio bases cannot be silently equated.
